chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Ubeyda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

A woman was brought to Ali (peace be upon him) along with a man who had been immoral with her. So she said, 'He coerced me, by Allah, O Commander of the Faithful!' So he staved off the Penalty (Hadd) from her. And if these people were asked about that, they would say, 'Do not ratify (her testimony),' even though the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) had done it.

key_terms.دَرَأَ: To stave off or avert (a punishment)
key_terms.فَجَرَ: To be immoral or commit fornication/adultery

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali rule on a woman's testimony when she claimed coercion in sexual immorality?
ai.summary: In this foundational case from al-Kafi, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) demonstrated judicial flexibility by accepting a woman's testimony of coercion to exempt her from the Hadd punishment for fornication, prioritizing her specific circumstance over rigid application. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the Imam's discretion (Ijtihad) can override general consensus when addressing unique evidentiary contexts, highlighting the dynamic nature of early Islamic legal theory.
